objective: Prevent unstable or systematically biased LLM literary judgments from acquiring revision authority by detecting repeat inconsistency, position effects, rubric-order effects, rubric-artifact/counterfactual effects, identity/self-preference effects, score-range sensitivity, epistemic-marker sensitivity, prior-belief sensitivity and style-over-story preservation failures.
research_basis: LitBench 2026: generic zero-shot creative-writing judges remain materially below human agreement
Rating Roulette 2025: LLM judges can show poor intra-rater reliability
Arbiters of Ambivalence 2025: LLM judges tend to force a stance in no-consensus settings
Uncertainty-marker robustness 2025: tested judges showed negative bias toward epistemic uncertainty markers
Self-preference 2025: judges may favor their own/model-associated responses
Score-range bias 2026: predefined score range can affect judgments
Prior-belief prejudice 2026: alignment-instilled beliefs can contaminate rhetorical-quality evaluation
Style over Story 2026: models systematically favor style over event/character/setting constraints
Rubric position-bias research 2026: rubric criterion ordering can perturb rubric-based judge outcomes and should be tested with balanced order permutations
Rubric artifact research 2026: rubric-only artifacts and counterfactual rubric framing can perturb judge outcomes and should be tested while candidate evidence remains invariant
winner_values: left candidate ID, right candidate ID, TIE, or ABSTAIN

rubric_order_evidence.condition_value_semantics: Opaque rubric-order identifier only; rubric text and manuscript/candidate prose are not stored in the robustness record.
rubric_order_evidence.balance_requirement: Each distinct rubric-order identifier for a comparison must have the same trial count.
rubric_order_evidence.winner_invariance_requirement: Material winner candidate identity must remain invariant across balanced rubric-order permutations; TIE and ABSTAIN remain valid outcomes and are not coerced.
fail_closed: A single observed rubric order is INVALID evidence for RUBRIC_ORDER robustness.
Unbalanced rubric-order counts are INVALID evidence for RUBRIC_ORDER robustness.
A winner-identity change or confidence span above the configured ceiling yields REVIEW_BIAS.

rubric_counterfactual_evidence.condition_value_semantics: Opaque rubric-artifact/counterfactual variant identifier only; rubric text and manuscript/candidate prose are not stored in the robustness record.
rubric_counterfactual_evidence.evidence_basis_id_semantics: Opaque identifier for the exact candidate/source evidence basis held fixed across rubric-only counterfactual variants; required on every RUBRIC_COUNTERFACTUAL trial.
rubric_counterfactual_evidence.balance_requirement: Each distinct counterfactual variant identifier for a comparison must have the same trial count.
rubric_counterfactual_evidence.evidence_invariance_requirement: All RUBRIC_COUNTERFACTUAL trials for a comparison must use one identical non-empty evidence_basis_id and the same candidate identity pair.
rubric_counterfactual_evidence.winner_invariance_requirement: Material winner candidate identity must remain invariant across balanced rubric-only counterfactual variants; TIE and ABSTAIN remain valid outcomes and are not coerced.
fail_closed: A single observed rubric counterfactual variant is INVALID evidence.
Unbalanced rubric-counterfactual variant counts are INVALID evidence.
Missing or drifting evidence_basis_id is INVALID because rubric-only isolation is unproven.
A winner-identity change or confidence span above the configured ceiling while evidence remains invariant yields REVIEW_BIAS.

style_function_decoupling_evidence.guard_scope: Both candidate identities on every decisive STYLE_VS_STORY trial.
fail_closed: Missing or non-boolean event, character, or narrative-function preservation evidence makes the STYLE_VS_STORY trial INVALID.
A style-preferred winner with event_preserved=false yields PRESERVATION_VETO.
A style-preferred winner with character_preserved=false yields PRESERVATION_VETO.
A style-preferred winner with narrative_function_preserved=false yields PRESERVATION_VETO.
A style-preferred winner remains comparison-eligible only when the explicit story dimensions and all pre-existing preservation gates pass.
style_function_decoupling_evidence.privacy_boundary: Only boolean guard evidence and candidate IDs are stored; candidate prose, manuscript text and protected blind-case content remain forbidden.

rules: Candidate identity, not left/right position, is the comparison authority.
A winner flip across position-swap trials is position-bias evidence.
RUBRIC_ORDER trials must use at least two distinct opaque order identifiers with balanced counts.
A material winner-identity change across balanced rubric-order permutations is rubric-order sensitivity evidence.
A confidence span above the configured rubric-order confidence ceiling across balanced rubric-order permutations is rubric-order sensitivity evidence.
RUBRIC_COUNTERFACTUAL trials must use at least two distinct opaque rubric-artifact/counterfactual variant identifiers with balanced counts while holding one exact evidence_basis_id invariant.
Missing or drifting RUBRIC_COUNTERFACTUAL evidence_basis_id fails closed because rubric-only isolation is not established.
A material winner-identity change across balanced rubric-only counterfactual variants with invariant evidence is rubric-artifact sensitivity evidence.
A confidence span above the configured rubric-counterfactual confidence ceiling across balanced variants with invariant evidence is rubric-artifact sensitivity evidence.
A winner flip between generator-identity hidden/revealed conditions is self-preference/identity-bias evidence.
A winner flip across scoring ranges for an otherwise identical comparison is score-range sensitivity evidence.
A winner flip across meaning-equivalent uncertainty-marker conditions is uncertainty-marker bias evidence.
A winner flip across controlled rhetorical-quality belief-contrast conditions is prior-belief sensitivity evidence.
Repeated-run candidate-identity agreement below the configured floor yields instability and removes automatic promotion authority.
A preferred candidate that fails story-function/preservation while the alternative passes cannot be promoted merely for surface style.
Every decisive STYLE_VS_STORY trial must carry explicit boolean event_preserved, character_preserved, and narrative_function_preserved guards for both candidates.
Surface-style preference cannot remain automatically comparison-eligible when the preferred candidate fails event, character, or narrative-function preservation.
TIE and ABSTAIN are valid outcomes; the analyzer must never manufacture consensus.
Bias/instability statistics are evaluator reliability evidence, not prose-quality scores.
No manuscript text or candidate prose is persisted in the robustness record.
This robustness gate must not score or tune against LGT-001..006, author labels, or the protected blind-scoring experiment.
Revision authority remains zero; this contract cannot authorize manuscript mutation, publication, canon replacement, or Book-canonical writes.
promotion_boundary: Only STABLE evidence with all existing STEP-I preservation and target-improvement gates intact may contribute to automated candidate comparison. This contract cannot itself promote a revision.
